title: Authorisation and fire-scene release
audience: Coordinators, supervisors and trained workers who may be asked about, triage, refer or document cleaning and salvage after a fire or smoke event. Not a qualification or authority to enter a fire-damaged building, release it, or certify it as safe.
learningOutcomes: Identify the authority that controls a fire-damaged property and the written release it has given, and refuse work that is not released.

instruction.heading: Scope and authority
instruction.body: This lesson teaches how to check who controls a fire-damaged property and whether that authority has released it for the work proposed. It does not grant authority to enter, release, re-occupy or disturb a fire-damaged property. Completing it does not give a licence, certificate or approval.

instruction.heading: Authorisation and fire-scene release
instruction.body: Authority and access are assessed only after access, permitted tasks and responsibility are established. An owner may ask for immediate salvage while the fire investigation or structural survey has not released the premises. Ask who controls access, what has been formally released and which safety reviews are still open. Customer urgency is never a substitute for verification. Check the written authority that controls the property, the scope of permitted access and any restriction on disturbing contents. Where clearance is ambiguous, remain outside and request confirmation from the responsible authority. Before acting, record the site evidence, the decision owner, the uncertainties and any specialists needed. An unverified scene-release claim must stop work. In training, compare three mock release documents and decide which, if any, permits the proposed activity. Record why keys or a verbal permission on their own are insufficient. The handover from this stage should state the scope, the observations, the unresolved hazards, the consent or authority held, the responsible professional and the next review step.

procedure: Stop work and remain outside any area the controlling authority has not released.
Ask who controls access, what has been formally released, by whom, and which safety reviews remain open.
Read the written release and check the scope of permitted access and any restriction on disturbing contents.
Record the decision owner, the uncertainties and the specialists needed before any step is taken.
If clearance is ambiguous, refuse entry and request written confirmation from the responsible authority.
Issue a handover that states the scope, the observations, the unresolved hazards, the authority held, the responsible professional and the next review step.

workedExamples.situation: An owner asks for immediate salvage while the fire investigation has not released the premises.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What must happen before any work starts?
workedExamples.reasoning: Ask who controls access and what has been formally released. Customer urgency is not verification. Remain outside, record the request and ask the responsible authority for the written release.

workedExamples.situation: A customer offers the keys while a structural inspection is still pending.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Can the keys act as the release?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Keys show access, not release. Refuse entry, record the outstanding clearance and escalate to the responsible authority.

equipmentAndPpe: No entry PPE is issued under this lesson. Entry is not permitted until a written release is confirmed.
Authority and access register, copy of the written release and decision log kept with the job file.

commonErrors.error: Starting salvage because the owner is anxious, without a written release from the controlling authority.
commonErrors.prevention: Verify the release in writing. Customer urgency does not substitute for it.

commonErrors.error: Accepting keys or a verbal assurance as the release.
commonErrors.prevention: Keys show access, not release. Ask for the written release and record who gave it.

commonErrors.error: Accepting a release from someone who does not control the site.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm who controls the site and record the controlling party and the scope of the release.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This lesson does not grant authority to enter, release or re-occupy a fire-damaged building. Completing it does not give a licence, certificate or approval.
NSW asbestos guidance states that clean-up should only begin after properties are made safe. The same sequence governs fire-scene work: the release comes first.
Western Australian guidance advises not entering a property until authorities confirm it is safe.

qualityStandard: The learner identifies who controls access and what has been formally released, and refuses work where the release is missing or unclear.
The learner separates keys and verbal permission from a written release.
documentationEvidence: Authority and access register: controlling party, written release (copy held), scope of permitted access and the date verified.
Stop-work note listing the open safety reviews and the referral made.
summary: Fire work starts with the written release from the controlling authority. Urgency is not verification.
Keys and verbal assurances are not a release.
Where clearance is ambiguous, remain outside and ask the responsible authority in writing.

knowledgeChecks.question: An owner asks for immediate salvage while the fire investigation has not released the premises. What must happen first?
options: Start salvage, because the owner has the keys and the owner is the one who pays for the work
Ask who controls access and obtain the written release from the responsible authority before any work.
Start with the rooms the owner says are safe, since the owner knows the building best of all

knowledgeChecks.question: Which document shows that a fire-damaged site has been released for work?
options: A written release from the authority that controls the site, stating its scope
The owner's verbal assurance that the site is fine

officialReferences.title: Managing asbestos in emergencies and disasters
officialReferences.covers: Read directly 2026-11-03. Asbestos-containing material directly impacted by fire is considered friable. Clean-up should only begin after properties are made safe. All fire-damaged asbestos removal works must be undertaken by Class A licensed asbestos removalists. Where professional help is not available, it is safest to leave asbestos where it is or keep it contained until a professional can help. NSW guidance only; other jurisdictions not covered.

officialReferences.title: Asbestos safety after an emergency or disaster
officialReferences.covers: Read directly 2026-11-03. Do not enter a property until authorities confirm it is safe. Avoid spreading ash or moving debris by sweeping or vacuuming. Never use high-pressure sprays; dampen ash and debris lightly to limit dust. Wear a P2 face mask and protective clothing such as sturdy boots and gloves, even if unsure whether asbestos is present. Contact a competent person or licensed asbestos assessor before clean-up starts. If asbestos is confirmed, a licensed asbestos removalist carries out the clean-up. Urgent removal: notify WorkSafe and submit the notification within 24 hours. Emergency work still requires a clearance. WA guidance only.

moduleAuthority.heading: Module authority and restricted work
moduleAuthority.body: Fire-scene release, structural and utility isolation, asbestos assessment and removal, and some waste handling are restricted to competent and, where the law requires, licensed people, and may be controlled by fire investigators, the police, structural engineers, utilities or the building owner. Insurer and owner permission do not replace a release from the authority that controls the site. Where that authority is not identified, do not proceed.

stopWorkAndReferral: Stop and refer when the release from the controlling authority is missing or unclear.
A stop-work decision is correct, so record it and restart only once the competent party confirms the scope in writing.
